A1.justification: Both PDFs present the same Stepping Stone Plus (SSP) research work. All 11 pages, including equations, figures, tables, and end matter, support reliable comparison. Neither supplied PDF contains an appendix.

before.justification: Section 5 reports original SSP experiments on S4, MS3, and AVSS, including benchmark results, component ablations, sensitivity analyses, and qualitative examples.

after.justification: Section 5 retains the original SSP benchmark results and analyses in Tables 1–2 and Figures 5–8.

M1.justification: Section 4 and Algorithm 1 retain identical optical-flow pre-masking, textual prompts, visual-textual alignment, post-masking, and training objectives.

E1.justification: Both versions use S4, MS3, and AVSS with the same single-source, multi-source, and semantic segmentation coverage. No dataset, task, or test scenario is added or removed.

E2.justification: Table 1 retains the same comparator rows, including AAVS, Save at both resolutions, TeSO, and AVS-Mamba. The cross-attention and AAVS comparisons in the supplementary analyses also remain unchanged.

E3.justification: Section 5.1 retains identical data splits, mIoU and F-score metrics, batch size, training epochs, and learning-rate schedules. The ablation and sensitivity-analysis settings also match.

E4.justification: Table 2's component ablations, Figure 5's loss-weight sensitivity analysis, Figures 6–7's prompt-quality analyses, and Figure 8's segmentation examples are identical.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests. Statistical reporting remains unchanged.

E6.justification: All numerical results and qualitative findings match. For example, Table 1 reports identical SSP mIoU/F-score values of 85.4/93.3 on S4, 72.3/84.6 on MS3, and 50.1/54.5 on AVSS.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions and Equations (1)–(5) are identical. No formal assumptions, derivations, theorems, or proofs are added, removed, or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same claims about optical-flow prompting, complementary textual prompts, visual-textual alignment, the post-mask objective, and superior segmentation performance.

C2.justification: The explanations of optical flow's limitations with stationary sounding objects, moving silent objects, and rapid motion are unchanged, as are the interpretations of how textual prompts compensate.

D1.justification: Sections 3–5.1 retain identical backbone choices, preprocessing, prompt wording, loss weights, and training details. No reproducibility information or code/data access instructions are added or removed.

R1.justification: Section 2, the positioning relative to AAVS and earlier prompt-based approaches, and all 56 references are unchanged.

P1.justification: The author order changes from Peng Gao followed by Yujian Lee to Yujian Lee followed by Peng Gao, retaining their equal-contribution markings. The arXiv version/date stamp is updated; the prose and section organization are unchanged.

P2.justification: Figures 1–8, Tables 1–2, Algorithm 1, captions, and page layout are unchanged. Pages 2–11 have identical rendered images.

improvement.justification: The only changes are the ordering of two equally contributing authors and the arXiv version/date stamp. Scientific content, evidence, reproducibility information, and readability remain unchanged, establishing no meaningful difference in overall paper quality.
